records.label: instance terminated via SIGKILL (zombie reaped by parent — isolation confirmed)

findings: WITHDRAWN: the round-24 run used GET (no body/method) — all its abort conclusions are void.
Termination left the busy state within sampling precision (0.0s observed) — this is an observation at probe polling granularity, NOT a claim that all in-flight tool side effects had ceased.
Turn 1 after abort: model reply NEVER delivered (no P0_DONE), yet the assistant message is FLAGGED completed — 'completed' is not evidence of delivery.

SCOPE LIMIT (per review): the second, proactively-sent abort proves only that an UNBOUND abort can kill whichever turn is running at arrival — it is NOT a full fault injection of an old request delayed in-flight and landing later; that deeper window remains unproven.
The destructive-window evidence justifies conservative resume gating; it does not characterize every late-arrival pattern.
POST /shutdown returning HTML only proves THIS path has no such API — not a general statement about graceful stop.
This environment: SIGTERM ignored for 12s, only SIGKILL terminated the CLI (zombie reaped via /proc) — environment-specific, not generalizable.
Mock boundary: the mock cannot react to cancellations; delivery evidence comes from the real opencode server's own status/message records.
